# OpenMarkdown Editor

> `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` is a live-preview Markdown editor built on [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/). Headings, lists, tables, math, Mermaid diagrams, callouts and YAML properties render in place, and the Markdown shows under the caret. It edits the Markdown source text itself, for a lossless round-trip: open and save without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was. When you edit, only what you touched changes, with a few exceptions, each pinned by a test.

Package: `@openmarkdown-dev/editor`, MIT, ES modules with TypeScript declarations. Framework-free: mount it from plain JavaScript, React or any other framework.

## Install

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor
```

## Minimal usage ([Your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor.md))

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

let file = openMarkdownFile(new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/notes.md")).arrayBuffer()));
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: file.text }));

const bytes = saveMarkdownFile(editor.getDoc(), file); // write these back
```

## Examples
- [Plain HTML](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/html-script/): One HTML file that loads the editor from a CDN with `<script type="module">` and mounts it: no framework and no bundler, but the package must be on the CDN.
- [React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/react/): The editor inside a React component: mounted in `useEffect`, destroyed on unmount, its text held in React state so the rest of the app can read and replace it. It uses the plain API; there is no React wrapper to install.
- [Reading mode](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/read-only/): Open a document read-only in reading mode, then switch to live preview or plain source with `setMode`. The document, selection and undo history stay as they were.
- [Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/theming/): Light and dark follow the host's colour scheme through `configureEditorEnvironment`, and the editor's colours, fonts and corners are restyled with `--ome-*` custom properties set on `.ome-root`. No stylesheet to import.
- [UI language](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/language/): The editor draws a few words of its own: the find panel, property controls, button tooltips. Pick their language (English, Chinese, Japanese or Korean) with `configureEditorEnvironment({ language })`; the document text is yours and never translated.
- [Image upload](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/image-upload/): Paste or drop an image and the editor hands its bytes to your `uploadImage` callback, which stores them and returns the URL or path to link. The document needs no path, so this works for a CMS field or any text kept in a database. `resolveImage` maps the link back to a URL the page can load. Here the "upload" stays in the browser tab.
- [Tables, diagrams and math](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/tables-diagrams-math/): Tables you edit cell by cell where they sit, Mermaid diagrams and LaTeX math rendered in place. The diagram and math renderers load only when a document first needs them.
- [Save and load](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/save-load/): Read a file's bytes with `openMarkdownFile`, give the editor its text, and write it back with `saveMarkdownFile`, which keeps the file's BOM and line endings. The page compares what Save would write with what was opened, byte by byte: open a file and save it without editing, and it is the same bytes. A file that is not valid UTF-8 is refused instead of opened.
